title: ECG Fundamentals
overview: This module covers the fundamental concepts of ECG interpretation, including heart anatomy, electrical conduction, and basic rhythm recognition. You'll learn about the cardiac cycle, electrode placement, and how to read a basic ECG strip.
objectives: Understand heart anatomy and electrical conduction system
Identify normal ECG components (P, QRS, T waves)
Recognize basic cardiac rhythms and their characteristics
Interpret basic ECG measurements and intervals

steps.title: Initial Assessment
steps.description: A 45-year-old male presents with chest pain. What is your first priority?

options.description: ECG should be obtained within 10 minutes of arrival
options.feedback: Correct! ECG is essential for chest pain evaluation and should be obtained immediately.

options.description: Chest X-ray can wait until after ECG
options.feedback: ECG should be obtained first for chest pain assessment.

options.description: IV access is important but ECG comes first
options.feedback: ECG is the priority for chest pain assessment.

steps.title: ECG Interpretation
steps.description: The ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. What does this indicate?

ecgData.ST Changes: ST elevation in II, III, aVF

options.description: ST elevation in inferior leads suggests inferior MI
options.feedback: Correct! ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF indicates inferior STEMI.

options.description: Anterior MI would show ST elevation in V1-V4
options.feedback: Incorrect. Anterior STEMI shows ST elevation in V1-V4, not inferior leads.

options.description: ST elevation is not normal in this context
options.feedback: Incorrect. ST elevation in this clinical context is concerning for MI.

pretest.question: What does ECG stand for?
pretest.explanation: ECG stands for Electrocardiogram, which is the graphical representation of the heart's electrical activity.

pretest.question: Which lead is placed on the right arm?
pretest.explanation: RA stands for Right Arm, which is one of the limb leads in a standard 12-lead ECG.

pretest.question: What does the P wave represent?
pretest.explanation: The P wave represents atrial depolarization, which occurs when the atria contract.

posttest.question: What is the normal duration of the QRS complex?
posttest.explanation: The normal QRS complex duration is 0.06-0.10 seconds (60-100 milliseconds).

posttest.question: Which wave represents atrial depolarization?
posttest.explanation: The P wave represents atrial depolarization, which occurs when the atria contract.

posttest.question: What is the normal PR interval?
posttest.explanation: The normal PR interval is 0.12-0.20 seconds (120-200 milliseconds).

posttest.question: Which leads are considered the limb leads?
options: Both I, II, III and aVR, aVL, aVF
posttest.explanation: The limb leads include both the standard leads (I, II, III) and the augmented leads (aVR, aVL, aVF).

title: Cardiac Rhythm Recognition
description: Identify and interpret various cardiac rhythms
overview: This module focuses on recognizing different cardiac rhythms, from normal sinus rhythm to life-threatening arrhythmias. You'll learn to identify rhythm patterns and understand their clinical significance.
objectives: Recognize normal sinus rhythm and its variations
Identify common arrhythmias and their characteristics
Distinguish between atrial and ventricular rhythms
Understand the clinical significance of different rhythms
Apply systematic approach to rhythm analysis

steps.title: Rhythm Identification
steps.description: The patient's ECG shows an irregular rhythm with no P waves. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.description: Irregular rhythm with no P waves is characteristic of AF
options.feedback: Correct! Atrial fibrillation is characterized by irregular rhythm and absent P waves.

options.description: Sinus rhythm would have visible P waves
options.feedback: Incorrect. Sinus tachycardia would have regular rhythm with visible P waves.

options.description: VT would have wide QRS complexes
options.feedback: Incorrect. VT would have wide QRS complexes, not narrow ones.

pretest.question: What is the normal heart rate range for adults?
pretest.explanation: The normal resting heart rate for adults is 60-100 beats per minute.

posttest.question: Which rhythm is characterized by irregular rhythm and absent P waves?
posttest.explanation: Atrial fibrillation is characterized by irregular rhythm and absent P waves.
